newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bratsk official confirms no strike on protest day.
newsitem.headline: Bratsk official confirms no strike on protest day.

text.p: Workers at Russia's Bratsk aluminium smelter who join nationwide protests against wage and pension arrears on Thursday will not do so during the work day and output will not be disrupted, a top Bratsk official said.

The official, who did not wish to be named, said on Wednesday that the plant's trade union and top management had written to President Boris Yeltsin to confirm that output would not be disrupted. A copy of the letter was obtained by Reuters.

Interfax news agency quoted the Mining and Metallurgical Trade Union, which in turn quoted Bratsk trade union deputy chairman Mihkail Gribachyov, as saying workers wanted to show solidarity with protestors across the country but that output would not be disrupted.
About 20 million protesters, backed by Russia's communist opposition, are expected by union officials to protest against massive backlogs in wages and pensions on Thursday.

The Bratsk official said it was possible that smelter workers whose wives are, for example, unpaid schooteachers might choose to join their spouses in protests at the end of the work day. But he said Bratsk employees would not take part in any protests during the work day.
"There are not and will not be any output disruptions -- that is certain," the official said.
Bratsk, the world's largest aluminium smelter, has forecast its 1997 primary aluminium output to rise one percent to 790,685 tonnes from 783,130 tonnes in 1996.
